content:
Maya: Anyone else seeing apiserver 502s in eu-central1? Started ~10:02 UTC, spikes every ~30s
ops-alert: ALERT: apiserver-frontend eu-central1 502 spike — incident#1234 (p95 latency 2.4s)
Jordan: controller-manager logs show leader-election churn, a bunch of controllers reporting failed syncs
Priya: we kicked off a huge GPU batch in that region around 09:55, could be node churn + IO pressure :eyes:
Miguel: checked etcd VMs — iostat looks terrible on sda2, avg-cpu ~90% and high await. WAL writes backing up
Miguel: ```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
sda 0.00 0.00 5.00 450.00 160.00 46000.00 202.00 22.30 180.00 4.00 176.00 0.50 90.00
```
Maya: kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-apiserver-eu-1 | tail shows a lot of "etcdserver: request timed out" and rpc latency spikes
Priya: this smells like small disk IOPS tier for etcd on those instance types. We saw similar when GPUs scaled up last quarter
Jordan: short term: can we pause the GPU autoscaler for that job and drain the new nodes?
Miguel: scaling down autoscaler now (scaling policy job-gpu-batch -> desired=0). Also opening ticket to bump etcd disk IOPS on the three voters — will take ~90s to reattach faster volumes
deploy-bot: scaled deployment job-gpu-batch to 0 (requested by Miguel)
Maya: after scale-down the 502s dropped but leader election still flapping. controller-manager logs: "error retrieving leader election record: failed to renew lease: context deadline exceeded"
Priya: changing --leader-elect flags mid-incident is risky. But maybe increase lease duration in next rollout to tolerate short IO spikes
Jordan: we should avoid flag churn. Alternative: move apiserver traffic to replicas in other AZs/regions and reduce pressure on that etcd quorum temporarily
Miguel: added apiserver replica in eu-central1-b and updated LB endpoints — propagation in ~20s
Maya: metrics look much better now, p95 latency back to baseline. Keeping watch for 15m before closing incident :thumbsup:
Priya: Follow-ups: 1) enforce minimum etcd disk IOPS for regions with GPU autoscaling 2) autoscaler guardrail to cap concurrent node adds 3) run a chaos test for mass node provision to validate control-plane resilience
Jordan: I'll draft the runbook update and add a canary job for large node launches. Putting notes in #eng-sre-postmortems
Miguel: I'll create the infra ticket to bump disk IOPS and add autoscaler limit, include cost delta estimate
Maya: thanks all — reopen if errors return
